role.altitude: The optometrist keeps examining, diagnosing, deciding treatment, prescribing, fitting and counselling; typing device values, notes, orders and standard answers shrinks.
skills_to_grow: Validating scribe notes and drafted answers quickly and well
role.ambitious_version: An optometrist who spends the saved minutes per patient on explaining the findings.

tasks.short: Have pre-tests run, analyze test results and images, compare with earlier visits, decide diagnosis and treatment plan, explain it, write the record note and refer where needed.

steps.what: Optometry assistant runs pre-tests (autorefraction, eye pressure, OCT, fundus photo) and types the values into the record
Optometrist analyzes test results and images on screen
Optometrist compares results with earlier visits by paging through the record
Optometrist decides the diagnosis and develops the treatment plan
Optometrist explains the findings and plan to the patient
Optometrist writes the record note with findings and plan

loop.input: The recording of the consultation (with the patient's agreement) and the structured test results in the record.
loop.output: A draft note in the practice's format: history, findings, diagnosis, plan.
loop.check: Values come from the structured results, not from the recording; the optometrist reads each draft against the findings and the plan explained to the patient, corrects it, and types the note when the draft misses or changes a finding; a monthly sample of notes is audited for omissions.
loop.stop: One draft per consultation; if the optometrist rejects it, the note is written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields cover values but not the history and reasoning told in the room.

steps.what: Optometrist writes the referral letter to the ophthalmologist when needed

loop.input: The validated record note and the structured test results for this visit.
loop.output: A draft referral letter with reason, findings and urgency.
loop.check: Every value must match the record, and the reason must match the plan in the validated note; the optometrist reads the reason and urgency against the findings and edits the letter.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template holds the values; the reason for referral needs a few sentences.

steps.what: Optometrist checks the final referral letter: findings, reason and urgency match the note, and the addressee is the right ophthalmologist
Optometrist sends the checked referral letter to the ophthalmologist

approvals.approved_version: The referral letter with findings, reason and urgency exactly as checked by the optometrist in s7b, sent once to the named ophthalmologist; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Pre-test devices write their values and images straight into the practice record ({OTHER}), and a progression view shows eye pressure, refraction and retinal thickness over earlier visits. An ambient scribe drafts the note from the recorded consultation, with values taken from the structured results, and the optometrist corrects and saves it; referral letters are drafted from the validated note; the optometrist edits, checks and sends each one. Analysing results, diagnosis, the plan and the talk with the patient stay with the optometrist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Device values were retyped and notes typed after each patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Eye devices export to practice systems; certified scribes draft notes for clinicians to validate.
tasks.still_hard: Reading images and judging progression is the optometrist's call.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a subtle change that means a referral.
tasks.altitude: A few minutes per patient go back to the patient; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether drafted referrals carry the findings the hospital needs.

evidence.claim: An ambient scribe records the consultation and the clinician validates the note before it goes into the record.
Across 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (29%).
A product drafts referral letters for clinicians.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI, including testing and monitoring after updates.

assumptions: Boundary: from pre-tests to the record note and referral; the eye examination itself and treatment are outside.
Input contract for s1 and s3: devices export values and images with patient id to the practice record; fallback is typing.
Input contract for s6: the consultation is recorded only with the patient's agreement; without it the note is typed.
The 29% note time cut from the case is used as the s6 saving.
Analysis, diagnosis and explaining keep their full time; the assistant's time is outside the optometrist's savings.

s3 keeps 40 for reading the progression view; s6 keeps 70 from the 29% case cut; s7 keeps 70 because the reason for referral is still written by the optometrist. The letter check (s7b) and send (s7c) take 1 each and keep their time; s3 gave 1 point of share to them.
unknowns: Whether the practice's devices can export to its record.
Share of patients agreeing to recording.
research_questions: How many scribe notes need content corrections?

already_counted.description: Optometrist reads and corrects each drafted note.

incremental.description: Optometrist takes part in the monthly sample audit of scribe notes.
Optometrist asks each patient for consent to record and handles refusals.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older devices do not export, so earlier values are still paged through and s3 keeps 70, and half of patients decline recording, so s6 keeps 85 (4.1); high: connected devices and most consultations recorded (8.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the lens prescription, help choose frames and lenses, take fitting measurements, check and send the lens order, fit and adjust glasses and contact lenses, and record what was supplied.

steps.what: Optometrist prescribes the corrective lenses from the final refraction values
Optometrist helps the patient choose frames, lens types and coatings
Optometrist takes fitting measurements: pupil distance and fitting height
Optometrist checks the final lens order: prescription, lens choice and measurements fit this patient and frame, and the order goes to the right lab
Optometrist sends the checked lens order to the lab: typed into the lab's portal today, released from the record to the lab's ordering interface after the change
Optometrist fits and adjusts the eyeglasses at collection and checks vision
Optometrist fits contact lenses with trial lenses and follow-up checks
Optometrist records what was supplied and fitted in the record

approvals.approved_version: The lens order with prescription, lens code and fitting measurements exactly as checked by the optometrist in s4, sent once to the named lens lab's ordering interface; any change makes a new order that needs a new check.

tasks.design: The final refraction values set on a digital phoropter and the measurements from a centration device flow into the practice record ({OTHER}), so the prescription and order fields are filled, not typed. The optometrist checks the complete order and releases exactly that order to the lens lab's ordering interface ({PARTNER_PORTAL}); the supply record for glasses is filled from the order. Choosing frames, fitting glasses and contact lenses stay with the optometrist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were read from devices and typed twice: into the record and into the lab portal.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital phoropters and centration devices export values; lens labs accept orders by interface.
tasks.still_hard: Fitting and adjusting by hand for comfort.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the frame and lens a patient will actually wear.
tasks.altitude: Less typing per patient; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether order errors from retyping disappear.

evidence.claim: Digital phoropters and centration devices export measured values to practice systems, and lens labs take orders by interface.
The patient record, including prescriptions, is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from refraction results to the supply record; making the lenses is the lab's work and outside.
Input contract for s1: the final subjective refraction values set by the optometrist on the digital phoropter, not the autorefractor's estimate; fallback is typing.
Coverage: about 60% of practices' refraction lanes have a digital phoropter; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s5: the lab's ordering interface accepts prescription, lens code and measurements; fallback is the portal by hand.

Choosing and fitting keep their full time. s3 keeps 70: the device takes the measurements, but the optometrist still positions the patient and the frame. s5 keeps 10 for the release. s8 keeps 60: glasses fill from the order, but contact lens fits are recorded by hand.
unknowns: Devices in the practice and their export options.
research_questions: How many lens remakes come from order errors before and after?

already_counted.description: Optometrist checks transferred values against the device before signing the prescription.

incremental.description: Optometrist keeps lens codes mapped to the lab's catalogue.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a manual phoropter and no lab interface, so s1, s3 and s5 keep their time (1.5); high: 60% of lanes with a digital phoropter and a lab interface for most orders as assumed (15.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide the medication, check allergies and interactions, write and sign the prescription, send it to the pharmacy, explain its use and record it.

steps.what: Optometrist decides which medication to prescribe for the eye disease, where national rules permit
Optometrist checks allergies, current medication and interactions
Optometrist writes the prescription in the record
Optometrist checks the final prescription: drug, strength, dose, duration and patient, and the patient's chosen pharmacy; then signs it
Optometrist sends the signed prescription to the patient's pharmacy: by hand or fax today, electronically from the record after the change
Optometrist explains how and when to use the medication
Optometrist records the prescription and follow-up in the record

approvals.approved_version: The prescription with drug, strength, dose and duration exactly as checked and signed by the optometrist in s3b, sent once electronically to the patient's chosen pharmacy; any change needs a new check and signature.

tasks.design: Prescribing happens in the practice record ({OTHER}) linked to the national drug database, which checks allergies, interactions, contraindications and doses when the medication is chosen; the optometrist reviews any warning. The prescription is filled from the record, signed by the optometrist and sent electronically to the patient's pharmacy, and the record entry is created from it. Choosing the medication and explaining its use stay with the optometrist; nothing is prescribed without the signature.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication lists were checked by asking and reading, and prescriptions were written on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Drug databases provide rule-based medication checks in prescribing software.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right drug for this patient.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing side effects against the patient's other conditions.
tasks.altitude: Fewer checks by hand; prescribing rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether fewer optometry prescriptions need a call-back.

evidence.claim: A national drug database checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software does not prescribe.
Whether optometrists may prescribe medication, and which, is set by national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the medication decision to the record entry; dispensing is the pharmacy's work and outside.
Input contract for s2: the patient's current medication and allergies in the record, from the patient and, where linked, the pharmacy; fallback is asking the patient.
Input contract for s4: an electronic prescription channel to pharmacies; fallback is paper.
Applies only where national rules let optometrists prescribe.
The decision and explanation keep their full time.

s3 keeps 50: patient and drug details fill from the record. s3b, the check and signature, keeps its time. s4 keeps 20 for choosing the pharmacy and the release. s6 keeps 50: the prescription entry is created, but the follow-up plan is written by the optometrist.
unknowns: Whether the practice's record links to the national drug database.
research_questions: How many medication warnings change the prescription?

incremental.description: Optometrist keeps favourite prescriptions and follow-up texts current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: no electronic channel to the pharmacy, so s4 keeps 100, and medication lists are often missing, so s2 keeps 70 (16.0); high: linked drug database and electronic channel as designed (24.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Educate and counsel patients on contact lens care, visual hygiene, lighting and safety, answer follow-up questions, give written instructions and record the counselling.

steps.what: Optometrist educates and counsels patients on contact lens care, visual hygiene, lighting and safety, and shows lens handling
Optometrist answers patients' follow-up questions by phone
Optometrist writes replies to written follow-up questions

loop.input: The patient's written question and the practice's library of approved patient leaflets.
loop.output: A draft reply citing the leaflet paragraphs it uses.
loop.check: Every statement must cite an approved leaflet paragraph, or the draft is not offered; the optometrist reads each cited paragraph to see that it supports the statement and fits this patient's lens type; questions about symptoms or personal treatment get no draft and are written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions are free text; a leaflet list still has to be matched to the question.

steps.what: Optometrist checks the final reply: each statement fits the question and the patient's lens type, and it goes to the right patient
Optometrist sends the checked reply to the patient
Optometrist picks the care leaflet for the patient's lens type and adds personal notes; today the instructions are written out
Optometrist checks the leaflet and notes before sending: right lens type, notes fit this patient, right patient
Optometrist sends the checked leaflet to the patient from the record
Optometrist records the counselling in the record

approvals.approved_version: The reply exactly as checked by the optometrist in s2c, sent once to this patient; any change needs a new check.
The care leaflet for this lens type with the optometrist's notes exactly as checked in s3b, sent once to this patient from the record; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Approved care leaflets per lens type sit in the practice record ({OTHER}) and are sent to the patient from it after the optometrist checks the leaflet and notes, and a counselling template records which advice and leaflet were given. Written follow-up questions get a draft reply built only from approved leaflets, with every statement cited; questions about symptoms get no draft, and the optometrist edits, checks and sends every reply. Counselling and showing lens handling stay face to face.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were handed out on paper and the same questions answered from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice records send documents to patients; language models draft answers limited to approved texts.
tasks.still_hard: Getting patients to follow lens hygiene at home.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a nervous first-time wearer how to put in a lens.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; written follow-up takes less time.

reach.task: Answer patient questions at the desk

evidence.claim: Guideline-based patient information texts are published by professional bodies with the patients' federation, a model for an approved leaflet library.
A chatbot facing patients must disclose that it is AI; here drafts go only to the optometrist.
Health data are special-category data; a DPIA is expected before drafting replies from patient messages.

assumptions: Boundary: from counselling to the record entry; treatment is outside.
Input contract for s2: a leaflet library approved by the practice's lead optometrist; fallback is writing replies.
Coverage: about half of follow-up questions arrive in writing (s2b, s2c, s2d); phone calls (s2) stay as they are. s2b keeps 50 for reading each draft and its cited paragraphs.
Counselling face to face keeps its full time.

s3 keeps 40 because the leaflet replaces writing out instructions, but the optometrist still picks it and adds notes. s4 keeps 80: the template records which leaflet was sent, but the counselling note is still written by the optometrist.
unknowns: How many follow-up questions arrive per week and by which channel.
research_questions: How many drafted replies are sent with few edits?

incremental.description: Optometrist keeps the leaflet library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few written questions fit the leaflets, so s2b keeps 80, and many patients need instructions written for them, so s3 keeps 70 (6.1); high: leaflets cover most questions and lens types (10.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
